correctness.rationale: The derivative is a bijection for arbitrary q>=2; a duplication inserts k zeros in one zero run. Exactly intersecting descendant sets correspond to legal transfers of k zeros. Reduced quotient vectors differ by a unit transfer, and the indexed modular sum changes by a nonzero value along any edge. Active words have at most n-2k+1 runs; inactive words have no neighbors. A q-independent K-clique witnesses equality. Both standalone direct-ball and composition-graph checkers passed. Universal quantifiers rely on the written proof, not finite enumeration.

evidence: Jain et al. 2016 construct fixed-length duplication-correcting codes and reduce errors to zero-block insertions.
Results concerning several duplication events or unbounded correction do not automatically partition all length-n words into the clique-minimal number of single-error correcting sets.
The published edge-count theorem has the same object and entire q,k,n parameter range but proves total edges and unique shared descendants, not coloring.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A code construction, even one correcting arbitrarily many errors, does not alone give a disjoint global K-codebook covering with K equal to the clique number. The present proof explicitly exhibits both the optimal covering colors and a K-clique; no inspected stronger result includes that assertion.

value.rationale: The invariant is the minimum number of disjoint error-correcting codebooks covering every q-ary word for a canonical single tandem-duplication channel. The theorem gives the exact answer uniformly across all alphabet sizes, duplication lengths and source lengths, a linear-time coloring, a matching unavoidable clique, and the exact edgeless threshold. This is structurally different from counting channel outputs, edges, or finding one feasible code. It does not overclaim maximum code sizes.
